pairs.evidence: src/features/settings/sub_byom/libs/useByomSettings.ts:161 applies an edited BYOM policy in place as bare unversioned JSON (src-tauri/db/src/byom.rs:305) that no audit row cites (src/lib/bindings/ProviderAuditEntry.ts:6), and src-tauri/engine/src/failover.rs:770 silently drops blocked providers so an emptied chain surfaces as the generic src-tauri/src/engine/runner/mod.rs:2398 message - re-anchored 2026-10-12 (failover.rs moved to engine crate in 9708af6d23)

techniques.evidence: src/features/settings/sub_byom/libs/useByomSettings.ts:161 saves the policy directly with no diff/approval step; src-tauri/db/src/byom.rs:305 overwrites one settings key with no version, so src/lib/bindings/ProviderAuditEntry.ts:6 can name a rule but never the policy version that served a call

src-tauri/engine/src/failover.rs:770 filters blocked providers with no empty-chain check (src-tauri/src/engine/runner/mod.rs:2067 consumes it unchecked), so 'no candidate survives the cascade' reaches the user as src-tauri/src/engine/runner/mod.rs:2398 'All providers failed or have open circuit breakers' - a policy outcome disguised as a transport failure
